recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is for the core spec. If this validation behavior is still reproducible, pursue it in the Java validator project with a minimal Questionnaire/QuestionnaireResponse reproduction, as the Jira comment and later Zulip guidance indicate.
issue_request: FHIR-20550 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Questionnaire issue raised against STU3 and applied for R5. It reported that SDC validation of questionnaireresponse-sdc-example-ussg-fht-answers incorrectly produced "Item has answer, even though it is not enabled" for item 2.1.1.4.1.1.1 because the Questionnaire evaluator ignored context and picked the wrong item. The Jira resolution was auto-approved, with a later editor comment saying to create a GitHub issue if the problem still existed.
initial_application: No FHIR-20550-tagged source commit was found in HL7/fhir history, and this checkout does not contain the Java validator/evaluator implementation or the diagnostic string. The relevant USSG-FHT Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse examples were already present in source before the issue.
additional_context: Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini, and the referenced USSG-FHT examples remain listed in the current example lists. Current Questionnaire source includes later enableWhen/linkId/context guidance from related, separately audited Questionnaire issues. Zulip records similar "Item has answer, even though it is not enabled" reports as validator/IG-support issues, including a 2021 SDC enableWhen validator discussion and a 2026 recommendation to file remaining problems against the Java validator repository.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current FHIR spec source does not contain an incorrect Questionnaire rule or stale example that can safely resolve this validator-evaluator report; changing the active examples or duplicating enableWhen prose would not address the root cause.
